deep.reconstruction:
This page is a raw observation log. It contains no derivation; the only numbers that can be worked through are time intervals and sums of pairs of readings. My reading of the entries (interpretation is mine):

(A) Wire-transit timings. Column 1 is headed 18.32 (I read this as 18h 32m). It lists the seconds 7.0, 15.0, 26.0, 33, [3]8.?, 45, 52, 4.5, 11.
- Successive differences: about 8, 11, 7, 5, 7, 7, 12.5, 6.5 s.
- The top of column 3 is headed 59' and lists 15.5, 22.3, 35.3, 42.5, 48.0, 54.4, 0|1.?, 13.4, 21.3.
- Its differences: 6.8, 13.0, 7.2, 5.5, 6.4, ~6.6, ~12.4, 7.9 s.
- The two interval patterns are nearly identical: a long gap, then four or five short gaps, then another long gap. This is the signature of a multi-wire reticle with unequally spaced wires. So these are times of an image crossing nine wires of a transit-type telescope, read from a seconds clock.
- The lower part of column 1 is a slower transit with the minutes written in the margin: 52m 40.2, 56.2; 53m 21.3, 36.2, 48.5; 54m 1.5, 17.2, 42.9; 55m 0; 56m 21.3.
  - Its intervals are about 16, 25, 15, 12, 13, 16, 26, 17 s. This is the same wire pattern, stretched by a factor of roughly 2.
- Column 2, lower block: 59.4, 11.5, 20.9, 31.8, 44.0, [46m] 4.5, 18.0. This is a partial transit with the same structure.
- A ratio of interval patterns like this would serve to check the wire distances or the rate of the moving image. That purpose is my inference; the page states none.

(B) Meteorological and instrument readings.
- The pairs 17.8 / 19.6 and 18.0 / 19.5 are most plausibly two thermometers.
- The entries 27.10.4 and 27.11.38 are most plausibly barometer readings in Paris inches and lines: 27" 10.4''' and 27" 11.38'''.
- The entries 300.4.31 and 320.46 look like divided-circle readings: 300°4'31" and 320°46'.
- Beside these are small integers (30, 26, 33/33, 28/29; and 28, 28, 32, 31). Below them are pairs (46.3, 69.2), (47.8, 67.6) and (45.8, 67.2). These read like the two ends of a level bubble.
  - Sums: 115.5, 115.4, 113.0.
  - Half-differences: 11.45, 9.9, 10.7 divisions.
  - That is, the bubble centre and the inclination.

(C) The sketch and note at the bottom.
- The sketch shows a forked, pronged mark on a post, i.e. the target (Ziel).
- The note reads: 'Ziel 4'' westl. / Bilder wechselsweise erschein[en] 2'' östl.' In translation: the target appears 4 seconds of arc to the west; the (double) images appear alternately 2'' to the east.
- This is a qualitative record of an image displacement. In the Dioptrik context it probably concerns a test of an objective or prism producing alternating or double images.
- The small '26 / 4' at the foot is an unexplained scrap of arithmetic.

Context from the next page: the next page records a distance BA and compares a measured value with 'theoretisch' values. It evaluates 19*(1/2 - 1/sqrt(8n^2-4)): for n = 3/2 the factor is 0.23274, and for n = 1.52 it gives BA = 4.5076. So this page appears to supply the observational side of a dioptric measurement. Nothing on this page itself is theoretical.

The interval patterns are internally consistent across the transits.
